reason: I already pay for Cursor/Copilot and my first reaction to any new AI coding tool is 'why add this?' Loom's shared-context pitch is clever, but my team runs one primary agent, not three, and I buy on engineering-lead authority — my authority says the incumbent already covers it. $30/seat is another daemon, another config, another bill for marginal gains.
objection: We already pay for GitHub Copilot Enterprise; why add another tool and another monthly bill when the context sharing Loom offers doesn't solve a real pain for my single-agent workflow?
would_change_my_mind: If my team standardized on three or more different agents and context actually broke between them, so Loom solved a live friction instead of a hypothetical one.
